name: Christmas
seo_title: Christmas Charcuterie Board Ideas: 10 Boards (Wreath, Tree, Cocoa + More)
description: 10 Christmas charcuterie board ideas: a wreath, a Christmas tree board, a hot cocoa board, candy and dessert boards, Christmas Eve and Christmas morning boards, plus how much to buy.
answer: The Christmas charcuterie boards people remember are shaped: a wreath of rosemary, salami and cheese around a bowl, or a tree built in rows on a rectangle. Use red and green on purpose (pomegranate, rosemary, cranberries, green olives), add one luxury cheese, and plan about 2 oz each of cheese and meat per guest.

ideas.title: The Christmas Wreath Board
ideas.text: A ring of rosemary sprigs, folded salami, cubed cheese, green grapes and pomegranate around a bowl of whipped feta or cranberry sauce. Every photo of it gets shared.

ideas.title: The Christmas Eve Board
ideas.text: A cozy board to graze through the evening: a baked Brie with cranberry, Stilton and port, prosciutto, pears and gingersnaps.

ideas.title: Christmas Charcuterie Cups
ideas.text: A rosemary-and-salami skewer, cheddar and Manchego cubes, three crackers and a few cranberries in a clear cup. Tie a red ribbon around each one.

ideas.title: The Christmas Tree Board
ideas.text: Cheese, salami and rosemary built in rows into a tree shape on a rectangle board, with a star cut from cheese on top. The same layout works as a vegetable tray.
ideas.on_it: Cheddar and pepper jack cubes · salami · rosemary sprigs · green olives · cherry tomatoes · grapes · crackers · a cheese star

ideas.title: The Hot Cocoa Board
ideas.text: A hot chocolate bar on a board: marshmallows, peppermint, whipped cream and cookies around a pot of cocoa. Good for a cookie swap, a movie night or Christmas Eve.
ideas.on_it: Hot cocoa · marshmallows · whipped cream · crushed candy canes · chocolate chips · caramel · cookies · cinnamon sticks

ideas.title: The Holiday Entertaining Board
ideas.text: A full party board in red and green, with a luxury cheese, cranberry, rosemary and pomegranate. Sized for the party, not for before a meal.

ideas.title: The Candy Board
ideas.text: Christmas candy sorted by color in rows and piles: peppermints, chocolate, gumdrops and candy canes. No cooking, and it's the board kids remember.
ideas.on_it: Peppermints · chocolate truffles · gumdrops · candy canes · chocolate-covered pretzels · red and green candies

ideas.title: The Christmas Cookie Board
ideas.text: Five or six kinds of Christmas cookies fanned in rows, with dark chocolate, strawberries, clementines and a dip. Plan 3 to 4 cookies per guest, or 2 to 3 after a big dinner.
ideas.on_it: Sugar cookies · gingerbread · shortbread · chocolate crinkles · biscotti · dark chocolate · strawberries · clementines

ideas.title: The Vegan Holiday Board
ideas.text: Vegan brie with rosemary, a cranberry walnut spread, pomegranate and spiced nuts. Built so a vegan guest can eat everything on it, and everyone else won't notice.

ideas.title: Christmas Morning Bagel Board
ideas.text: Set it out the night before, minus the fresh things, and brunch is done while the presents get opened.
ideas.on_it: Bagels · cream cheeses · smoked salmon · capers · red onion · tomato · cucumber · fruit

ideas.title: Charcuterie Skewers
ideas.text: A board's worth of bites on sticks: tortellini, mozzarella, salami, olives and tomato. Easy to eat with a drink in hand, and no crowd around one board.
ideas.on_it: Salami · mozzarella balls · tortellini · olives · cherry tomatoes · basil · rosemary

shapes.name: Wreath Board
steps: Put a small bowl in the middle of a round board and lay a ring of rosemary sprigs around it.
Build the ring out with folded salami, cheese cubes, grapes and green olives, alternating colors.
Dot pomegranate seeds and cranberries on top, and tie a ribbon bow at the bottom.

shapes.name: Christmas Tree Board
steps: On a rectangle, lay a pretzel rod or cheese block as the trunk at the bottom.
Build rows that get shorter as you go up: crackers, salami, cheese cubes, grapes, rosemary between each row.
Top with a star cut from a slice of cheddar.

shapes.name: Candy Cane Board
steps: Draw a J shape on a long board with a line of crackers.
Fill it with alternating stripes of white (Brie, mozzarella) and red (salami, strawberries, red peppers).
Frame it with rosemary and green grapes.

plan.what: Order specialty cheese and buy boards, cups, picks and ribbon.
Buy crackers, nuts, jams and dried fruit. They keep.
Buy cheese, meat and fresh fruit. Pick rosemary.
Cut cheese, fold meats, make skewers. Cover and chill.
Take cheese out of the fridge and build the board: bowls, cheese, meat, then fruit, rosemary and the garnish.

faq.q: How do you make a charcuterie wreath?
faq.a: Put a small bowl in the center of a round board, lay a ring of rosemary around it, then build the ring out with folded salami, cheese cubes, grapes and olives. Finish with pomegranate seeds and a ribbon bow.

faq.q: How much charcuterie do I need for a Christmas party?
faq.a: As an appetizer before dinner, about 2 oz of cheese and 2 oz of meat per guest, plus 6 to 8 crackers. If the board is the party food, plan 3 oz of each; if it's dinner, 4 oz. From 20 guests, add 10%.

faq.q: How far ahead can I make a Christmas charcuterie board?
faq.a: Build it up to 4 hours ahead, cover it tightly and keep it in the fridge; add crackers just before serving. Take hard cheeses out about an hour before serving and soft ones like Brie 20 to 30 minutes before.

faq.q: What are the best Christmas cheeses?
faq.a: Stilton with port is the English classic, Brie baked with cranberry is the crowd favorite, and an aged cheddar or Manchego is the easy all-rounder.

faq.q: Can a charcuterie board be a Christmas gift?
faq.a: Yes: a wooden board, a hard cheese that travels well, a salami, a jar of fig jam and crackers make a great hostess gift. Skip soft cheeses if it won't be opened the same day.

faq.q: How do you make a Christmas tree charcuterie board?
faq.a: Build rows on a rectangle board, getting longer toward the bottom: cheese cubes, folded salami, rosemary and olives. Add a trunk of crackers and a star cut from cheese on top.

faq.q: What goes on a hot cocoa board?
faq.a: Hot cocoa, marshmallows, whipped cream, crushed candy canes, chocolate chips, caramel, cinnamon sticks and cookies. Keep the cocoa warm in a slow cooker.

faq.q: What's a good Christmas morning board?
faq.a: A bagel board: bagels, two or three cream cheeses, smoked salmon, capers, red onion, tomato and fruit. Set out everything but the fresh items the night before.

mistakes.lead: Too much red and green filler.
mistakes.text: Pomegranate, rosemary and cranberries are enough color. Plastic decorations and food that's only there for color get left on the board.

mistakes.lead: Building the wreath or tree too early.
mistakes.text: Shaped boards lose their shape as the cheese softens. Prep everything ahead, but assemble within an hour of the party.

mistakes.lead: Party amounts before a big dinner.
mistakes.text: Before Christmas dinner, 2 oz each of cheese and meat per guest is enough. Save the bigger board for the party.
A hot cocoa board or a candy board keeps the kids away from the expensive cheese.
